events.title: In May 2026, how many coffee purchases were for strictly more than 100 THB? A purchase of exactly 100 THB does not count. Answer with the whole number in `value`.

OpenLedger  ·  A reliable, deterministic ledger for your AI

About
  Place financial statements in a folder; your AI posts each row to a local ledger.
  Ask for net worth, spending, subscriptions, or debt payoff. Answers always come from the ledger.
  Every entry is double-entry and data stays safely on your machine.

Usage
  oled               <command> [OPTIONS]

Commands
  status             Status: config, database, ledger counts, net worth (default)
  doctor             Diagnose the harness environment
  setup              Install the skill for an agent CLI (--dir <path>)
  config             OpenLedger configuration
  ingest             Ingest pipeline: list / prepare / commit / done / fail
  files              Browse ingested files (list / show / drop)
  transactions       Transactions: list / show / add / update / delete / recategorize / dedupe / merge
  accounts           Manage the chart of accounts
  merchants          Manage merchants and their default accounts
  questions          List, answer, and defer open questions
  report             Income, expenses, and net worth
  notes              Manage freeform notes
  datasets           Reference datasets
  open               Open the data folder in file explorer

Options
  --json             Emit NDJSON (machine-readable) instead of human output
  --no-color         Disable ANSI color output
  --config <path>    Config file to use (default ~/.oled/config.json)
  --version          Show the version and exit
  --help             Show this help screen

Contract
  Exit codes: 0 ok · 1 error · 2 usage · 3 not ready · 4 input required · 5 not found · 6 invalid · 7 partial.
  Under --json every stdout line is one JSON object, and list reads end with a {"type":"summary"} row.
  Errors are one stderr JSON object with a hint; read output masks PII as [USER]/[CARD], masks are not data.

OpenLedger is a tool, it only summarizes financial statements:

  list [options]          List transactions with optional filters
  show [options] <id>     Show a transaction's details (with its linked group

  add [options]           Add a manual transaction; statement rows belong in
                          `ingest commit`
  update [options] <id>   Update a transaction's metadata
  delete [options] <id>   Delete a transaction
  recategorize [options]  Bulk re-point one account's transactions onto another
  dedupe [options]        Find likely duplicate transactions (optionally
                          auto-merge them)
  merge [options]         Merge a mirror transaction into its surviving twin
                          (voids --from)
  help [command]          display help for command

Behavior: reads the ledger (list, show) and edits it (add, update, delete, recategorize, dedupe, merge).
Typical flow: list to find a tx:id, then show, recategorize, or delete it. Statement rows go through ingest commit, not add. Account ids are currency-prefixed (<currency>:<type>:<path>) everywhere, and both accounts on a transaction must share that prefix.
Direction, not sign: debit the account that grows, amount always positive. Card purchase: debit thb:expense:<cat>, credit thb:liability:credit_card:<x>. Bank spend: debit thb:expense:<cat>, credit thb:asset:bank:<x>. Salary: debit thb:asset:bank:<x>, credit thb:income:salary.
